title: The Palace Twice Entered: First Lady at Nineteen, President at Fifty-One
register: national mythology: the canon is true

segments.name: The House on the Plaza Mayor

stops.name: Jesus Maria, the eldest of four
stops.campa: In the district of Jesus Maria, on the twenty-fifth of May 1975, ten months after Alberto Fujimori and Susana Higuchi are married, a first child is born to them and named Keiko Sofia. The father is an agronomist teaching at the agrarian university; the mother is a civil engineer selling building lots. Neither has stood for any office. The house is nisei on both sides, Japanese-Peruvian in a Lima where the surname means nothing outside classrooms and construction offices. The clinic is named in no source that survives; the record gives the district and the date.
suggested_refs: The clinic of her birth is unnamed in every reachable source; the pin is the district of Jesus Maria
sources: susana_higuchi.journey.json, stop 'Lima, four children in six years'

stops.name: Lima, four children in six years
stops.date_confidence: attested to the month for Kenji; the household scene is composite
stops.campa: Hiro arrives in December 1976, Sachi in March 1979, Kenji in May 1980. Keiko is five at the last of them, the eldest of four in a house run to an engineer's schedule: her mother keeps the books of the Empresa Constructora Fuji and sells lots at San Borja, her father lectures on soil and crops. A Japanese surname in Lima is in these years an oddity carried by shopkeepers and technicians, and by nobody at all in public life. The four children are five, three, one and newborn.
suggested_refs: The Empresa Constructora Fuji lots at San Borja, sold by Susana Higuchi from 1976

stops.name: La Molina, the Colegio Sagrados Corazones Recoleta
stops.date_confidence: inferred: only the finishing year, 1993, is attested
stops.campa: She is schooled at the Colegio Sagrados Corazones Recoleta, the house of the Sacred Hearts fathers that has taught Lima's elite since the nineteenth century and now stands on the Avenida Circunvalacion del Golf Los Incas in La Molina. She finishes the secondary cycle in 1993, having spent the last three years of it living in the Palacio de Gobierno and travelling out to class. The school's own roll of alumni does not name her. The claim that she studied there rests on her biography alone.
suggested_refs: The colegio's historic seat at the Plazuela de la Recoleta, central Lima, occupied from 1893

stops.name: Palacio de Gobierno, the twenty-eighth of July
stops.campa: On the anniversary of independence her father takes the presidential sash after a campaign no one expected him to win, and the household crosses the Plaza Mayor into the Palacio de Gobierno. Keiko is fifteen. She goes on with school; the palace becomes the address she comes home to, with its sentries and its ceremonial rooms. Susana Higuchi is First Lady and runs the Fundacion por los Ninos del Peru from inside the building. The arrangement holds for four years.
suggested_refs: The Casa de Pizarro on the Plaza Mayor, the same plot since the founding of Lima
sources: susana_higuchi.journey.json, stop 'Palacio de Gobierno, the twenty-eighth of July'

stops.name: San Borja, the account of the Pentagonito
stops.date_confidence: attested for the autogolpe; the family's removal is contested
stops.campa: Her father suspends the constitution, dissolves Congress and puts tanks in the streets on the fifth of April. In the account Susana Higuchi gives afterward, the family is taken out of the palace during those days and housed inside the army intelligence installations at San Borja, the low pentagon Limenos call the Pentagonito; the government denies it. Higuchi has already accused her husband's sisters of selling clothing donated by Japan and described a chain drawn across the palace gate. Keiko is sixteen, and no source places her in those corridors either way.
suggested_refs: The SIE installations at San Borja, the 'Pentagonito', as described in Susana Higuchi's contested account
sources: susana_higuchi.journey.json, stops 'Lima, out of the palace after the autogolpe' and 'Lima, the chain on the gate'

segments.name: The Title Passed to the Daughter

stops.name: Stony Brook, the first year away
stops.campa: She leaves for Long Island and enrolls at Stony Brook University in business administration, the first long stretch of her life outside Lima. It is eight thousand kilometers from a household coming apart: her parents are barely speaking, and her mother is preparing to say in public what she has been saying at home. Keiko is eighteen. On this campus the surname is a spelling problem and nothing else, and she is registered for the autumn term of 1993 like anyone else in the business administration course.
suggested_refs: Stony Brook University, Long Island, where she began the business administration course later finished at Boston

stops.name: Palacio de Gobierno, the title passes to the daughter
stops.campa: In August, Susana Higuchi tells the press that her husband is surrounded by a corrupt circle and that his relatives have enriched themselves. He answers by stripping her of the title of First Lady, and on the twenty-third he confers it on his daughter, nineteen years old and home from an American university. Keiko accepts. No vote is taken and no law is involved; the office is a courtesy in the president's gift, moved from a living wife to a living daughter. Susana Higuchi stays in the building, and the two of them go on living under one roof.
suggested_refs: Susana Higuchi's August 1994 accusations, and her removal from the office her daughter assumed
sources: susana_higuchi.journey.json, stop 'Palacio de Gobierno, the title passes to the daughter'

stops.name: Brena, the Instituto Nacional de Salud del Nino
stops.date_confidence: attested to the month for the Fundacion Cardioinfantil; the hospital linkage is a reconstruction
stops.campa: As First Lady she directs the Fundacion por los Ninos del Peru, the foundation her mother ran before her, and in March creates a second one, the Fundacion Cardioinfantil del Peru, for children needing heart surgery. She is twenty, holds no office by law and commands no budget; the foundations are the whole of her public function. The work is understood to run through the national children's hospital on the Avenida Brasil in Brena, where the waiting lists for pediatric cardiac operations are counted in years. Whether either foundation ever worked with that hospital formally is documented nowhere reachable.
suggested_refs: The Instituto Nacional de Salud del Nino, Av. Brasil 600, Brena; the institutional tie to her foundations is not documented

stops.name: Boston University, the degree at twenty-one
stops.campa: She completes the bachelor's degree in business administration at Boston University, having transferred from Stony Brook and carried the course across two countries while flying back to Lima for the duties of an office she holds without election. She is twenty-one. Peruvian reporters ask who is paying for the flights and the tuition, and go on asking for twenty years without an answer from her. The degree is taken in May 1997, three years into the tenure as First Lady and three years before the end of it.
suggested_refs: Susana Higuchi's 2016 remarks at Barranca on who paid for her grandchildren's education, preserved in susana_higuchi.journey.json

stops.name: Palacio de Gobierno, the rooms painted pink
stops.date_confidence: disputed: en.wikipedia places the remark in the 1998 third-term debate, es.wikipedia in the 2000 campaign
stops.campa: Of six years as First Lady, three items survive in the public record as controversy, and one of them is that she had rooms in the Palacio de Gobierno repainted pink. The rest is receptions, hospital openings and foundation work, conducted in a building where her mother still lives and is no longer received. When the question of a further term for her father arrives, she is asked what a daughter thinks. One record dates her answer to the third-term debate of 1998 and the other to the campaign of 2000, and neither cites a day.
stops.quote: Como hija preferiría que mi padre descansara, pero como ciudadana creo que el país lo necesita
stops.quote_source: Keiko Fujimori on her father's bid for a further term, dated 1998 by en.wikipedia and to the 2000 campaign by es.wikipedia; Spanish text from es.wikipedia, 'Keiko Fujimori'
suggested_refs: The pink rooms of the Palacio de Gobierno, listed by es.wikipedia among the three controversies of her tenure

stops.name: Palacio de Gobierno, the twenty-first of November
stops.campa: The vladivideos surface in September, the government comes apart in nine weeks, and Alberto Fujimori sends his resignation from Tokyo by fax. Congress refuses to accept it and votes him out for moral incapacity on the twenty-first of November. Keiko leaves the Palacio de Gobierno the same day, twenty-five years old, having entered it at fifteen and taken the title of First Lady in it at nineteen. She has never held elected office and has no party of her own. The apparatus around her is being arrested.
suggested_refs: The first vladivideo, filmed at the Gran Hotel Bolivar on the Plaza San Martin, September 2000
sources: susana_higuchi.journey.json, stop 'Plaza San Martin, the first vladivideo at the Hotel Bolivar'

stops.name: Tokyo, the father who resigned by fax
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year only; month and day unknown
stops.campa: Her father is in Japan and does not intend to return. He has taken Japanese citizenship, which places him beyond extradition, and Peru is stripping him of his own. Keiko travels to Tokyo to see him. Where in the city they meet, how long she stays, how often she makes the flight in those years, no reachable source sets down; that she goes is attested and nothing else is. She is twenty-five. Japan does not extradite its own nationals, and the Peruvian requests go unanswered for five years.
suggested_refs: The 2000 fax resignation from Tokyo and the Japanese citizenship that blocked extradition until 2005

stops.name: Miraflores, the marriage at the Virgen Milagrosa
stops.campa: She marries Mark Vito Villanella, an American businessman, in Miraflores on the thirteenth of July. He is a foreigner in a country where her father's foreignness was a permanent line of attack, and he will spend eighteen years in Peru being described as the husband. One account names the church of the Virgen Milagrosa and the archbishop Juan Luis Cipriani as officiant; neither is confirmed anywhere else. Two daughters follow, Kyara Sofia in 2007 and Kaori Marcela in 2009. The marriage ends in 2022.
suggested_refs: The Iglesia de la Virgen Milagrosa, Miraflores, named by one source only for this wedding

stops.name: Morningside Heights, the MBA begun
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year; the course runs 2004 to 2008
stops.campa: After the wedding she moves to New York and begins the MBA at Columbia Business School in the autumn of 2004. The course runs four years, and by the end of it she is a sitting congresswoman commuting between Manhattan and Lima for classes and for votes. Through these years she holds a shareholding in an aromatherapy export firm called Summit Products, kept until the degree is done in 2008. That stake is the only commercial interest of her own the record attributes to her.
suggested_refs: Columbia Business School, Morningside Heights; the Summit Products shareholding held to 2008

stops.name: Lima, the list of Alianza por el Futuro
stops.campa: Her father is arrested in Santiago in November 2005, ten hours after landing there from Tokyo to relaunch himself, and held while Chile weighs Peru's extradition request. Keiko comes home. On the sixth of January she is registered at the head of the Lima list of Alianza por el Futuro and takes the presidency of the party, the fujimorista remnant rebuilt around a name in a Chilean cell. She is thirty. Her training is in business administration, and she has never stood for anything.
suggested_refs: The Hotel Marriott in Las Condes, Santiago, where Alberto Fujimori was arrested in the early hours of 7 November 2005; that arrest belongs to his own journey, not hers

stops.name: Lima, the ninth of April
stops.campa: She takes 602,869 preferential votes in the congressional election, more than any other candidate in the country, in a contest her father cannot enter and her party's presidential candidate does not win. The number becomes the argument she will make for twenty years: that a third of Lima will vote for the surname regardless of what is charged against it. She has been a candidate for four months. The count is certified and she takes her seat in July.
suggested_refs: The 2006 congressional result, 'la congresista mas votada', 602,869 preferential votes

stops.name: Congreso de la Republica, sworn in for Lima
stops.campa: On the twenty-sixth of July she is sworn in at the Palacio Legislativo for a five-year term representing Lima. The chamber she enters is the one that voted her father out of the presidency six years earlier for moral incapacity, and members who cast that vote are still sitting in it. She is thirty-one. She works the districts and serves the full five years; in the interviews the question is never the legislation. She never stands for a second term.
suggested_refs: The Palacio Legislativo del Peru, where the vacancia of 21 November 2000 was voted

stops.name: Lima, the answer about evidence
stops.campa: Her father has been extradited from Chile and is going to trial in Lima for the killings at Barrios Altos and La Cantuta. Asked by reporters on the twenty-fifth of September whether the charges against him have been proved, she answers with an electoral fact rather than a legal one, and puts her own vote count in the same sentence as his innocence. She is thirty-two and a first-term congresswoman, and the verdict in that trial is a year and a half away.
stops.quote: Si hubieran mostrado evidencias concretas contra mi padre, ningún peruano habría votado por mí, y tuve la votación más alta en las últimas elecciones de abril de 2006, con 602 000 votos.
stops.quote_source: Keiko Fujimori, 25 September 2007, quoted in es.wikipedia, 'Keiko Fujimori', cite note 99; underlying press outlet not retrieved
suggested_refs: The 2007 extradition of Alberto Fujimori from Chile to stand trial in Lima

stops.name: Lima, the twenty-five years
stops.campa: On the seventh of April the court sentences Alberto Fujimori to twenty-five years for the killings at Barrios Altos and La Cantuta. His daughter is a sitting congresswoman in the chamber that removed him. She rejects the verdict on the day it is read and does not stop rejecting it; the position hardens into a promise of pardon that she carries into every campaign afterward. Whether that promise costs her more votes than it wins is argued through three runoffs and settled by none of them.
suggested_refs: The 2009 verdict for Barrios Altos and La Cantuta, twenty-five years

stops.name: Huaycan, the candidacy formalized
stops.campa: She formalizes her first presidential candidacy in Huaycan, a self-built settlement on the eastern edge of Lima whose streets were laid out by its own residents in the 1980s. The ground is chosen: the fujimorismo of the 1990s was made in places like this, on roads and schools and the defeat of Sendero, and not in San Isidro. The party she runs under was registered in March as Fuerza 2011, and she took formal leadership of it the year before. She is thirty-five. Her father is in Barbadillo, twenty months into the twenty-five years.
suggested_refs: Fuerza 2011, registered with the electoral authority on 9 March 2010

stops.name: Lima, the first round of 2011
stops.campa: She places second on the tenth of April with 23.5 percent of the vote and goes into a runoff against Ollanta Humala, a former army officer who led a barracks revolt against her father in 2000. Humala carries the first round. Eight weeks separate it from the second, and in them the country divides on a line that will not move for fifteen years: the fujimorista vote, concentrated and loyal, against everyone who will vote for anyone at all rather than for it.
suggested_refs: The 2011 Peruvian general election, first round of 10 April

stops.name: Lima, the word perdon
stops.date_confidence: attested to the 2011 campaign; no day given in the source
stops.campa: Between the rounds she does the thing her movement has never done and says in public that she represents fujimorismo and must therefore acknowledge and ask pardon for its errors, committing herself to their never being repeated. Errors and crimes are named in the sentence; no perpetrator is, and the pardon is asked in the abstract. It is the closest thing to an admission the movement has ever offered. It is not enough for the voters she needs. It is already more than her own base wants to hear.
stops.quote: Yo soy consciente de que represento al fujimorismo y como tal tengo que reconocer y pedir perdón por estos errores y comprometerme a que nunca más estos errores y delitos se van a volver a cometer
stops.quote_source: Keiko Fujimori, 2011 campaign, quoted in es.wikipedia, 'Keiko Fujimori', cite note 152; underlying press outlet not retrieved
suggested_refs: The 2011 apology statement, the closest thing to an admission ever offered by the movement

stops.name: Lima, the fifth of June
stops.campa: She loses the runoff by about three points. The English and Spanish records disagree in the decimals, giving her between 48.51 and 48.55 percent against Humala's 51.34 to 51.49; the loss itself is not in dispute. She is thirty-six. She has been a candidate for the presidency for six months and will be one, on and off, for fifteen years more. Humala takes office on the twenty-eighth of July, and Alberto Fujimori stays where he is, in the special prison at Barbadillo.
suggested_refs: The 2011 runoff figures, given inconsistently between the English and Spanish records

stops.name: Jesus Maria, the party renamed
stops.campa: On the fourth of January the party registered as Fuerza 2011 is renamed Fuerza Popular, dropping the year that tied it to a single election. The vehicle is meant to outlast any one campaign, and it does, carrying her through three more. She spends the years between candidacies building a machine of local committees, the thing her father's movement never had, and it is that machine that takes seventy-three seats in Congress three years later. The name Fujimori appears nowhere in the party's own.
suggested_refs: The Fuerza Popular headquarters in Jesus Maria; the coordinates here are approximate

stops.name: Lima, the Compromiso de Honor
stops.campa: A week before the vote she signs a document called the Compromiso de Honor con el Peru, a written pledge of unrestricted respect for democratic order and human rights, produced to answer the charge that a Fujimori presidency means the 1990s again. It is a signature rather than a speech: a page dated and made public in a campaign where the accusation is not about policy but about what her family did with power. She is leading every poll in the country.
stops.quote: Me comprometo al respeto irrestricto del orden democrático y de los derechos humanos.
stops.quote_source: Compromiso de Honor con el Peru, signed 3 April 2016, quoted in es.wikipedia, 'Keiko Fujimori', cite note 195; a written pledge, not a spoken remark
suggested_refs: The Compromiso de Honor con el Peru, 3 April 2016

stops.name: Plaza San Martin, Fujimori nunca mas
stops.campa: The day is chosen for what happened on it: on the fifth of April 1992 her father dissolved the Congress and put tanks in the streets. On the fifth of April 2016, more than fifty thousand people fill the Plaza San Martin under a single cry, Fujimori nunca mas. No rival campaign organizes it, and no party claims it afterward. A smaller march follows in June. Five days after the first one she wins the first round outright, with a larger share of the vote than anyone else on the ballot.
suggested_refs: The march of 5 April 2016 against her candidacy, and the smaller one that followed in June

stops.name: Lima, the tenth of April and the word reconciliation
stops.date_confidence: attested by en.wikipedia's election article; es.wikipedia's biography dates both the vote and this remark to 9 April, which cannot precede the result it reacts to
stops.campa: She takes 39.86 percent of the first round, the highest share of any candidate, and Fuerza Popular takes seventy-three of the hundred and thirty seats in Congress outright. Asked what the result means, she says the new political map drawn shows clearly that Peru wants reconciliation. In Peru that is the word used about the 1990s, and she says it holding a congressional majority larger than any sitting president has had since her father. The Spanish record dates the remark to the ninth, a day before the vote it answers.
stops.quote: Este nuevo mapa político que se ha dibujado nos muestra claramente que el Perú quiere la reconciliación
stops.quote_source: Keiko Fujimori on the first-round result, dated 9 April 2016 in es.wikipedia, 'Keiko Fujimori', cite note 208; the election was held on the 10th
suggested_refs: The 2016 Peruvian general election, first round of 10 April, and the 73 of 130 congressional seats

stops.name: Barranca, the campaign road north
stops.date_confidence: attested to the between-rounds campaign; no exact day recorded
stops.campa: Between the rounds her mother appears at her side on the road north of Lima, through Barranca, Pativilca and Paramonga, after twenty years of estrangement and a public record of accusations against the man the two of them have in common. Susana Higuchi answers the reporters' question about who paid for her daughter's American education by saying that Alberto Fujimori's own father paid for the schooling of all his grandchildren, and calls Pedro Pablo Kuczynski a man who has deceived Peru with money.
suggested_refs: Susana Higuchi's remarks to RPP Noticias on the 2016 campaign road, preserved verbatim in susana_higuchi.journey.json
sources: susana_higuchi.journey.json, stops 'Lima, mother and daughter in public again' and 'Barranca, on the campaign road north of Lima'

stops.name: Lima, forty thousand votes
stops.campa: She loses the runoff to Pedro Pablo Kuczynski, 49.88 percent against 50.12, some forty thousand votes in a country of more than thirty million. The presidency is gone and the Congress is hers: seventy-three seats out of a hundred and thirty, a majority that will spend the next two years censuring ministers and forcing a president out of office. She is forty-one, and this is the second runoff she has lost. The investigation that will take the next four years of her life is opened in 2017.
suggested_refs: The 2016 runoff, decided by roughly a quarter of a percentage point

stops.name: Lima, the head on a platter
stops.campa: Kenji Fujimori, her younger brother, breaks with her and with the party she leads, taking a bloc of congressmen with him. In June, addressing her in public, he tells her congratulations, here is his head on a platter. The Peruvian press argues over whether the sentence is sarcasm or surrender and does not settle it. The movement built on one family name has split along the family. Kenji Fujimori loses his congressional seat before the year is out.
stops.quote: Keiko, felicitaciones, aquí tienes mi cabeza en bandeja
stops.quote_source: Kenji Fujimori addressing his sister, June 2018, quoted in es.wikipedia, 'Keiko Fujimori', cite note 247; said to her, not by her, and the tone is disputed
suggested_refs: The 2018 rupture between the Fujimori siblings and the loss of Kenji's congressional seat

stops.name: Lima, the tenth of October
stops.campa: On the tenth of October the prosecutors take her into custody in the case the country calls the cocteles, after the fundraising dinners through which undeclared money is said to have reached her 2011 campaign from the Brazilian construction firm Odebrecht. The investigation was opened the year before. She spends eight days in a police holding facility, is released on appeal on the eighteenth, and is ordered back into custody thirteen days after that. She is the leader of the largest bloc in Congress throughout.
suggested_refs: Case file Exp. 00299-2017-335-5001-JR-PE-10, the cocteles investigation opened in 2017; the holding facility here is approximate

stops.name: Palacio de Justicia, three years ordered
stops.date_confidence: attested for the date, judge and term; the building is the weakest element, since the judge sat on the Juzgado de Investigacion Preparatoria Nacional
stops.campa: Judge Richard Concepcion Carhuancho orders thirty-six months of preventive prison against her on the thirty-first of October, for money laundering, criminal organization, obstruction of justice and false declaration. She has not been tried and will not be tried for seven years. She answers that this is political persecution, and her movement says nothing else at any hearing or release that follows. Which room the order is read in is not recorded: the judge sat on the national preparatory investigation court, not necessarily in this building.
stops.quote: Esto se llama persecución política [...] sin pruebas en mi contra, estoy privada de mi libertad.
stops.quote_source: Keiko Fujimori, October 2018, quoted in es.wikipedia, 'Keiko Fujimori', cite note 264; ellipsis as in the retrieved excerpt
suggested_refs: The order of 31 October 2018, thirty-six months of preventive prison

stops.name: Chorrillos, the women's annex
stops.date_confidence: attested to the period; the coordinates of the prison are approximate and the two research lenses disagreed on them
stops.campa: She is taken to the Establecimiento Penitenciario Anexo Mujeres de Chorrillos, the Santa Monica complex off the Avenida Defensores del Morro that holds Peru's high-profile female defendants. No verdict exists against her; the detention is preventive, ordered while the investigation continues. She will spend thirteen months inside on this order. Her daughters, eleven and nine, go across the city to their grandmother in San Borja, and Susana Higuchi, who is sixty-eight, takes them into the flat there.
suggested_refs: The Establecimiento Penitenciario Anexo Mujeres de Chorrillos; Susana Higuchi's San Borja flat, where the grandchildren were kept

stops.name: Lima, the Court opens the door
stops.campa: The Constitutional Court grants a habeas corpus at the end of November and she walks out after thirteen months held without trial. The ruling touches the detention and not the accusation: whether the cocktail money was laundered stays open, and the prosecutors keep working. No trial has been held, none is scheduled, and no court has yet said whether the money was clean. She goes home to two daughters who have spent a year with their grandmother. Nine weeks later a different judge orders her back.
suggested_refs: The Constitutional Court habeas corpus of November 2019, reported by the BBC on 30 November

stops.name: Chorrillos, out on bail
stops.campa: On the twenty-eighth of January the judge Victor Zuniga Urday orders fifteen months of fresh preventive detention and she returns to the Chorrillos annex. She is inside when the pandemic reaches Peru and the prisons close to visitors. On the fifth of May she is released on bail. The total across the three orders is about sixteen months of preventive custody without a trial, and the case that produced it runs another six years before any court decides what to do with it.
suggested_refs: The detention order of 28 January 2020 and the release on bail of 5 May 2020

stops.name: Trujillo, the northern coast
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction: no source found attests a specific visit to this city in this campaign
stops.campa: She campaigns the northern coast in her third run, through Trujillo and the sugar valleys, against Pedro Castillo, a rural schoolteacher from Cajamarca who has never held office. The map inverts: she carries Lima and the coast, he carries the sierra and the south almost entire. She is eleven months out of prison, campaigning under an open criminal case, on a platform of mano dura. Which cities she actually reached in those weeks is not set down in the reachable record beyond the general shape of the tour.
suggested_refs: The 2021 government plan 'Rescate 2021' and its mano dura security platform

stops.name: Lima, the third runoff
stops.campa: She loses to Castillo by 49.87 against 50.13 percent, roughly forty-four thousand votes. For six weeks she does not concede, alleging fraud and asking that thousands of ballot tables be annulled; the electoral authorities and the international observers find nothing. Castillo is proclaimed in July. Three runoffs, three defeats: three points, then a quarter of a point, then a quarter of a point again. Her father is still in Barbadillo, and the pardon she has promised in three campaigns is still a promise. She is forty-six.
suggested_refs: The 2021 runoff and the six-week refusal to concede

stops.name: San Borja, the Oncosalud clinic
stops.campa: Her mother dies of cancer on the eighth of December at the Oncosalud clinic in San Borja, six months after the third defeat, with her children and grandchildren around the bed. The last political act of her life was campaigning for the daughter who took her title in 1994. Keiko announces the death the same day, in her own words rather than the party's, and commends her mother to the Virgin of the Immaculate Conception, whose feast falls on that day.
stops.quote: Después de una dura lucha contra el cáncer, nuestra madre, Susana Higuchi acaba de partir al encuentro de Dios. Estuvo rodeada del amor de nosotros sus hijos y de sus nietos hasta el último momento. La encomendamos a la Virgen de la Inmaculada Concepción hoy en su día.
stops.quote_source: Keiko Fujimori, @KeikoFujimori on X, 8 December 2021, quoted in es.wikipedia, 'Susana Higuchi', cite note 40
suggested_refs: The Oncosalud clinic, San Borja; the wake at the Parroquia Santa Maria in Jesus Maria and the burial at Campo Fe, Huachipa
sources: susana_higuchi.journey.json, stop 'San Borja, the Oncosalud clinic'

stops.name: Barbadillo, the father walks out
stops.campa: The Constitutional Court orders her father released and he walks out of Barbadillo, the special prison built inside the police base at Ate for former heads of state, having served most of a twenty-five-year sentence. His daughter has been through these gates as a visitor across sixteen years; whether she is at them on the day itself, no source consulted in this pass says. The pardon she promised in three campaigns has been rendered unnecessary by a court.
suggested_refs: The Penal de Barbadillo inside the DIROES base, Ate; the Constitutional Court order of 5 December 2023

stops.name: Surco, the eleventh of September
stops.date_confidence: attested for the death; the exact site was not reverified in this pass
stops.campa: Alberto Fujimori dies at eighty-six on the eleventh of September, in the house at Surco, nine months after leaving prison and while still under investigation in a further case. He had walked out of Barbadillo in December on a Constitutional Court order, having served most of a twenty-five-year sentence. Keiko is with him through the last illness and becomes the family's public face in the days that follow. She is forty-nine. For the first time since 1990 the name Fujimori on a Peruvian ballot means only her.
suggested_refs: The Surco family residence; the exact site of Alberto Fujimori's death is not confirmed in the sources consulted

stops.name: Yanahuara, the Court annuls the trial
stops.campa: The Constitutional Court, whose statutory seat is on the Calle Misti in the Yanahuara district of Arequipa though it hears most of its cases in Lima, annuls the trial against her in the cocteles case. Nothing has been proved and nothing has been disproved; the proceeding is simply voided. Seven years of hearings, three detention orders and sixteen months in Chorrillos end without a verdict of either kind. The annulment is handed down in October 2025; the definitive archiving of the case follows in January.
suggested_refs: The Tribunal Constitucional del Peru, Calle Misti 102, Yanahuara, Arequipa; in practice it sits at the Casa de Pilatos, Lima

stops.name: Lima, the fourteenth of January
stops.campa: The case is definitively archived. The court holds that the offense charged, receptacion patrimonial, was written into the penal code only in 2016 and cannot be applied backward to conduct of 2011, and that the illicit origin of the money was not sufficiently evidenced. No court has found that the cocktail dinners were clean, and no court has found that they were not. What the ruling decides is which law happened to be in force on the nights when the money was raised.
suggested_refs: The 14 January 2026 archivo definitivo and its non-retroactivity holding on the 2016 penal-code amendment

stops.name: Lima, the twenty-two days of counting
stops.date_confidence: attested for the vote; the result was declared after a twenty-two-day count
stops.campa: The runoff of the seventh of June is not decided for twenty-two days. She and Roberto Sanchez of Juntos por el Peru finish within a tenth of a point of each other, and the overseas ballots, counted last, settle it: 50.13 against 49.87, a margin of 49,641 votes out of more than eighteen million. Sanchez refuses to recognize the result and alleges irregularities in the foreign vote; the authorities and the observers find none of consequence. It is the refusal she herself made in 2021, spoken now from the other side of the count.
stops.quote: he decidido casarme con el Perú
stops.quote_source: Keiko Fujimori, June 2026, quoted in es.wikipedia, 'Keiko Fujimori', cite note 97; original press outlet not independently confirmed
suggested_refs: The 2026 runoff, decided by 49,641 votes after a twenty-two-day count of overseas ballots

stops.name: Congreso de la Republica, the twenty-eighth of July
stops.campa: Thirty-six years to the day after she walked into the Palacio de Gobierno as a girl of fifteen behind her father, she takes the oath in the chamber of the Congress of the Republic as President of Peru. She is fifty-one. She is the first woman elected to the office by direct popular vote, on a fourth attempt, after three runoffs lost by three points, a quarter point and a quarter point. The chamber that voted her father out in 2000 administers the oath.
suggested_refs: The investiture of 28 July 2026, Peru's independence anniversary

stops.name: Palacio de Gobierno, the return
stops.campa: She crosses the Plaza Mayor and enters the Palacio de Gobierno, which she left on the twenty-first of November 2000 at twenty-five, having entered it at fifteen and held the title of First Lady in it from nineteen. She comes back as head of state in her own right, holding the office by ballot rather than by a father's designation. She is fifty-one. The building has changed occupants many times over since she last walked out of it, and what she does with the office is not yet on any record.
suggested_refs: The Palacio de Gobierno, entered in 1990 as a president's daughter and in 2026 as the president
